subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should third-party plugin state remain globally plugin-scoped, become agent-scoped for cache use, or support an explicit choice between those scopes?
rationale: Current main deliberately places arbitrary plugin state in the shared database while reserving agent databases for agent-owned data; changing that boundary creates a permanent Plugin SDK and isolation contract that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Add explicit scopes
options.body: Extend the existing plugin-state API with explicit global and agent scopes and define lifecycle, isolation, quota, backup, and migration behavior for both.

options.title: Keep global namespaces
options.body: Retain shared plugin-state storage and require plugins to include agent identity in keys when agent separation is needed.

options.title: Require agent-local caches
options.body: Introduce an agent-only cache facade and prohibit cross-agent sharing through that API.

recommendation.title: Add explicit scopes
recommendation.body: Extend the existing plugin-state API with explicit global and agent scopes and define lifecycle, isolation, quota, backup, and migration behavior for both.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent involvement with the plugin-state storage boundary makes this person the best available owner for the public API direction.
